q.s: The earliest literary reference to the Andhras is found in which text?
q.x: The Aitareya Brahmana is the earliest literary reference to the Andhras; the Vinayavatthu is the first Buddhist text to mention 'Andhrapatha'.

q.s: According to the Mahabharata, the Andhras fought on the side of:
q.x: In the Mahabharata the Andhras fought on the side of the Kauravas.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the original trivarga of Purusharthas?
q.x: The trivarga was Dharma, Artha and Kama; Moksha was added later under Upanishadic ideas.

q.s: The Vedanga 'Nirukta' deals with:
q.x: Nirukta is etymology (Yaska); Shiksha is phonetics, Chandas metrics and Jyotisha astronomy.

q.s: Which Vedanga deals with metrics?
q.x: Chandas deals with metrics (associated with Pingala).

q.s: The Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna) is described in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
q.x: The Battle of Ten Kings is described in Mandala VII, one of the family books.

q.s: The Nasadiya Sukta on creation is found in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
q.x: The Nasadiya (creation) hymn is in Mandala X, the latest book of the Rigveda.

q.s: Which god became supreme in the later Vedic period?
q.x: In the later Vedic period Prajapati became the supreme god, while Indra and Agni lost their earlier importance.

q.s: Which is the oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Bhattiprolu, linked with the Yaksha kings Savaru and Kuberaka, is the oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The early relic stupa of Jaggayyapeta lies on the bank of which river?
q.x: Jaggayyapeta lies on the Krishna, not the Godavari.

q.s: Who wrote 'Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu', dedicated to Kakatiya Prataparudra?
q.x: Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu was written by Appayacharya; Jinasena wrote the Adipurana and Somadeva Suri the Yasastilaka Champu.

q.s: Ashoka's mission to Sri Lanka is described in which Pali chronicles?
q.x: The Sri Lankan Pali chronicles Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa describe Ashoka's mission to Sri Lanka.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Sri Lankan Pali chronicle?
q.x: The Arthashastra is Kautilya's Sanskrit treatise; the other three are Sri Lankan Pali chronicles.

q.s: Which of the following Ashokan edict sites is located in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Yerragudi (major and minor edicts) and Rajula Mandagiri (minor edict) are in Kurnool district; Brahmagiri, Siddapura and Maski are in Karnataka.

q.s: Which of the following southern kingdoms was NOT part of the Mauryan Empire?
q.x: The Pandya kingdom is named in the edicts as a neighbour, outside the empire.

q.s: Heliodorus, who set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, was the envoy of which Indo-Greek king?
q.x: Heliodorus was envoy of Antialcidas of Taxila at the court of the Sunga king Bhagabhadra.

q.s: Who wrote the 'Visuddhimagga'?
q.x: Buddhaghosa wrote the Visuddhimagga; Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakosa and Dinnaga founded Buddhist logic.

q.s: Who is regarded as the founder of Buddhist logic?
q.x: Dinnaga is regarded as the founder of Buddhist logic.

q.s: Which was the major centre of Jain art, noted for Tirthankara images, in the Gupta period?
q.x: Mathura was the leading centre of Tirthankara images; Sarnath was a Buddhist centre.

q.s: In Alauddin Khalji's market reforms, the 'Sarai Adl' was the market for:
o: Cloth, sugar, dry fruits and oil
q.x: Sarai Adl dealt in cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter and oil; the Mandi dealt in food grains.

q.s: Who founded the city of Jahanpanah in Delhi?
q.x: Jahanpanah was founded by Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Alauddin built Siri.

q.s: Which Sultan founded the city of Hisar?
q.x: Hisar was founded by Firoz Tughlaq; Sikandar Lodi founded Agra.

q.s: Whose token currency experiment failed because of widespread forgery?
q.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency failed through forgery.

q.s: The silver tanka of 175 grains was introduced by:
q.x: Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka (175 grains); the jital was copper.

q.s: Which is the earliest Indo-Islamic building in India?
q.x: The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Delhi (Aibak, 1198) is the earliest; Sultan Ghari (1231) is the first Islamic tomb.

q.s: The first double dome in India is found in the tomb of:
q.x: Sikandar Lodi's tomb has the first double dome; Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's tomb is the first octagonal tomb.

q.s: Under the Mughals, 'Khalisa' land referred to:
q.x: Khalisa was crown land whose income went straight to the treasury; it was not a jagir.

q.s: Which Mughal emperor gave Ram Mohan Roy the title 'Raja'?
q.x: Akbar II gave Ram Mohan Roy the title 'Raja'; Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after 1857.

q.s: The practice of 'Jharokha darshan' at the Mughal court referred to:
o: Emperor's daily appearance at a balcony
q.x: Jharokha darshan was the emperor's daily appearance at a balcony, begun by Akbar.

q.s: Who wrote 'Muntakhab-ul-Lubab'?
q.x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab is by Khafi Khan; the Alamgirnama is by Mirza Muhammad Kazim.

q.s: Who among the following wrote 'Subhadra Kalyanam'?
q.x: Tallapaka Timmakka, wife of Annamacharya, wrote Subhadra Kalyanam.

q.s: The dvipada 'Annamacharya Charitra' was written by:
q.x: Annamacharya's grandson Chinnanna wrote the Annamacharya Charitra.

q.s: Who is regarded as the first prominent Sufi in India, known as 'Data Ganj Bakhsh'?
q.x: Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh) of Lahore is regarded as the first prominent Sufi in India.

q.s: The Gaekwads of the Maratha Confederacy ruled from:
q.x: The Gaekwads ruled from Baroda; the Bhonsles from Nagpur, Holkars from Indore and Scindias from Gwalior.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a seat of a major house of the Maratha Confederacy?
q.x: The Bhonsles ruled from Nagpur, the Gaekwads from Baroda and the Holkars from Indore; Mysore was ruled by the Wodeyars and Haidar Ali.

q.s: In 1639 Francis Day obtained Madraspatnam on lease from:
q.x: Francis Day, with Andrew Cogan, got Madraspatnam from Venkatapati Raya III of Chandragiri in 1639.

q.s: Which became the first municipality in India (1687-88)?
q.x: Madras became India's first municipality in 1687-88.

q.s: Who was the French governor of Pondicherry from 1742 to 1754?
q.x: Dupleix (1742-54) followed Dumas and was replaced by Godeheu in 1754.

q.s: Who described the Revolt of 1857 as the 'First War of Indian Independence'?
q.x: The First War of Independence label is V.D. Savarkar's; R.C. Majumdar denied it was a national war of independence.

q.s: After the Battle of Plassey, Mir Jafar gave the Company the zamindari of:
q.x: After Plassey Mir Jafar granted the Company the zamindari of the 24 Parganas.

q.s: Who called Robert Clive a 'heaven-born general'?
q.x: William Pitt the Elder called Clive a 'heaven-born general'.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a condition imposed on an Indian ruler under the Subsidiary Alliance?
o: Freedom to negotiate with other states
Not employing other Europeans without Company consent
Accepting a British Resident at his court
Maintaining British troops on payment of subsidy
q.x: The ruler could not negotiate with other states without the Company's consent; the other three were conditions of the alliance.

q.s: Which Act made William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India?
q.x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Bentinck was the first.

q.s: Who was the first Viceroy of India under the Government of India Act, 1858?
q.x: The 1858 Act made Canning the first Viceroy.

q.s: The first Rampa rebellion (1879) was directed against:
q.x: The first Rampa rebellion in the Rampachodavaram Agency was against the mansabdar Madhava Bhupati and his taxes.

q.s: Which leader of the 1879 Rampa rising burnt the Addatheegala police station?
q.x: Darabandala Chandrayya burnt the Addatheegala police station.

q.s: 'Khuntkatti' associated with the Munda movement refers to:
q.x: Khuntkatti was the joint landholding of the Mundas; Abua Raj meant self-rule, the aim of Birsa's Ulgulan.

q.s: The term 'Dikus' in tribal movements referred to:
o: Outsiders such as moneylenders and traders
q.x: Dikus were outsiders – moneylenders, zamindars and traders.

q.s: Which Viceroy began financial decentralisation by giving provinces fixed annual grants for police, jails, education and roads?
q.x: Mayo's 1870 scheme gave provinces fixed grants; Lytton widened the provincial heads in 1877.

q.s: The Battle of Padmanabham, in which Vijayarama Gajapati Raju was killed, was fought in:
q.x: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794.

q.s: Who called the Trade Disputes Act, 1929 'the Slavery of India Bill'?
q.x: Motilal Nehru called it 'the Slavery of India Bill'.

q.s: The Royal Commission on Labour appointed in 1929 is known as the:
q.x: The Whitley Commission (1929, report 1931) included N.M. Joshi and Diwan Chaman Lal.

q.s: Jyotiba Phule's book 'Gulamgiri' means:
q.x: Gulamgiri means Slavery; Shetkaryacha Asud is The Cultivator's Whipcord and Satyashodhak Samaj the Society of Truth Seekers.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Minister (Premier) of the Madras Presidency under the Justice Party (1920)?
q.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar was the first, Dec 1920 to Jul 1921; Panagal Raja followed (1921-26).

q.s: The journals 'Andhra Patrika' and 'Bharati' were associated with:
q.x: Andhra Patrika and Bharati were Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's.

q.s: Who led the Guruvayur Satyagraha (1931-32)?
q.x: K. Kelappan led the Guruvayur Satyagraha; T.K. Madhavan was the key leader of Vaikom.

q.s: Who undertook temple-entry fasts at Nellore during 1946-48?
q.x: Potti Sriramulu undertook three temple-entry fasts at Nellore.

q.s: Which Round Table Conference was the only one attended by the Indian National Congress?
q.x: Congress attended only the Second RTC (1931), represented by Gandhi alone; Ambedkar attended all three.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Round Table Conferences is correct?
o: The Third RTC was held in 1930
Dr B.R. Ambedkar attended all three
q.x: Ambedkar attended all three; the Congress attended only the Second (1931) and the Third was in 1932.

q.s: National Youth Day in India (12 January) marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: National Youth Day, 12 January, is Vivekananda's birthday; he was born Narendranath Datta at Calcutta in 1863.

q.s: Sister Nivedita, the disciple of Swami Vivekananda, was originally named:
q.x: Sister Nivedita was Margaret Noble; Madeleine Slade was Gandhi's disciple Mirabehn.

q.s: Who represented Jainism at the World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago, 1893?
q.x: Virchand Gandhi represented Jainism; P.C. Mozoomdar the Brahmo Samaj and Anagarika Dharmapala Ceylonese Buddhism.

q.s: Who among the following did NOT attend the World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago, 1893?
q.x: Dayananda Saraswati had died in 1883.

q.s: The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was held at:
q.x: It met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay; it was shifted from Poona because of a cholera outbreak.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Simon Commission Report (1930)?
q.x: The Simon Commission did not recommend an Andhra province; it recommended provincial responsible government, separation of Burma and retained communal electorates.

q.s: Who persuaded Gandhi to come to Champaran at the Lucknow Congress of 1916?
q.x: Rajkumar Shukla, a local indigo cultivator, met Gandhi at Lucknow in December 1916; Gandhi reached Champaran on 10 April 1917.

q.s: In his statement of 20 February 1947, Attlee declared that the British would leave India by:
q.x: Attlee's deadline was June 1948; Mountbatten later advanced the transfer to August 1947.

q.s: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India on:
q.x: The Cabinet Mission was announced on 19 February 1946 and arrived on 24 March 1946.

q.s: Gandhi's weekly 'Harijan Bandhu' (1933) was published in which language?
q.x: Harijan was in English, Harijan Bandhu in Gujarati and Harijan Sevak in Hindi.

q.s: Civil Services Day is observed in India on:
q.x: 21 April marks Patel's address to the first IAS probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi, in 1947.

q.s: Who presided over the first session of the All India States People's Conference?
q.x: The first AISPC session was presided over by Diwan Bahadur M. Ramachandra Rao; Balwantrai Mehta was among its organisers.

q.s: Jawaharlal Nehru represented which Lok Sabha constituency?
q.x: Nehru represented Phulpur; he was PM from 15 August 1947 till his death on 27 May 1964.

q.s: Goa was made a full State by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 56th Amendment (1987) gave Goa statehood; the 12th made Goa, Daman and Diu a Union Territory.

q.s: How many seats did the Telugu Desam Party win in the 1983 Andhra Pradesh Assembly election?
q.x: The TDP, founded by NTR on 29 March 1982, won 202 seats in 1983.

q.s: Who was Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh when N.T. Rama Rao founded the TDP (29 March 1982)?
q.x: Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy was CM at the time; T. Anjaiah had been replaced earlier in 1982.

q.s: Article 371D, giving effect to the Six-Point Formula for Andhra Pradesh, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: Article 371D was inserted by the 32nd Amendment (1973); the Presidential Order of 1975 set up local cadres.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the procedure under Article 3 is correct?
o: The views of the affected state legislature are not binding on Parliament
A reference to the state legislature is needed even for a Union Territory
A fresh reference is needed for every amendment to the Bill
The views of the affected state legislature are binding on Parliament
q.x: Parliament need not accept the state's views; no reference is needed for a Union Territory or for each amendment.

q.s: The Lower Palaeolithic site of Attirampakkam is located in:
q.x: Attirampakkam is in Tamil Nadu; Hunsgi is in Karnataka and Didwana in Rajasthan.

q.s: Which of the following Lower Palaeolithic sites is NOT located in present-day India?
q.x: The Sohan valley is in Pakistan Punjab.

q.s: Which Ikshvaku king overthrew the last Satavahana ruler Pulomavi III?
q.x: Santamula overthrew Pulomavi III c. AD 225-230; Bodhisri's gifts at Nagarjunakonda fall under Virapurushadatta.

q.s: Coins of Simuka, the Satavahana founder, have been found mostly at:
q.x: Simuka's coins with the legend 'Siri Chimuka Sata' come mostly from Kotilingala in Karimnagar, Telangana.

q.s: Which school of art is noted for white marble reliefs full of movement narrating the Jatakas?
q.x: The Amaravati school is marked by movement and emotional expression in its narrative reliefs.

q.s: The rock-cut caves of the Pallava king Mahendravarman I belong to which century CE?
q.x: Mahendravarman I's caves are of the 7th century CE; his lion-pillared style was later taken up by the Telugu Chodas and Eastern Chalukyas.

q.s: The Pancharama temples are attributed to which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
q.x: Chalukya Bhima I built the Pancharamas; Vijayaditya II built the 108 Saiva temples.

q.s: The Mahadeva temple, called the 'Emperor among temples', built under the Kalyani Chalukyas is at:
q.x: The Mahadeva temple is at Itagi; Kasivishveshvara is at Lakkundi.

q.s: Which dynasty first made Telugu the royal and administrative language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit?
q.x: The Renati Cholas first used Telugu as the royal language, about five centuries before Nannaya.

q.s: Rani Rudrama Devi's death in 1289 is recorded in which inscription?
q.x: The Chandupatla inscription records her death; she died fighting the Kayastha chief Ambadeva.

q.s: The Vijayanagara amara-nayankara system after 1565 led to the rise of independent Nayaka states. Which of the following was NOT one of them?
q.x: Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi became Nayaka states; Warangal was the Kakatiya capital.

q.s: Which historian called the Vijayanagara state a 'segmentary state'?
q.x: Burton Stein called it a 'segmentary state'; Nilakanta Sastri called it a 'military administration'.

q.s: Chand Bibi was married to which ruler?
q.x: Chand Bibi of Ahmadnagar married Ali Adil Shah I of Bijapur; Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

q.s: The dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas was:
q.x: The Kakatiya dynastic deity was Svayambhu Shiva; Alampur and Srisailam were Kalamukha centres.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Kalamukha centre in the Kakatiya period?
q.x: Lepakshi is a Vijayanagara-period temple; Srisailam, Alampur and Vemulawada were Kalamukha centres.

q.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is credited with building 108 temples?
q.x: Vijayaditya II is credited with 108 temples, built in the Dravidian idiom.

q.s: The 'floating bricks' are a famous feature of which temple?
q.x: The Ramappa vimana was built with light floating bricks.

q.s: The AICC meeting of 1921 that launched the Tilak Swaraj Fund was held at:
q.x: The AICC met at Bezawada (Vijayawada) in March-April 1921.

q.s: After the 1964 split in the communist movement, which party was pro-China?
q.x: The CPI(M) was pro-China and the CPI pro-Soviet; Ravi Narayana Reddy stayed with the CPI.

q.s: The journal 'Grandhalaya Sarvasvam' of the Andhra library movement began in:
q.x: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam began in 1915; the first library conference was in 1913.

q.s: Who is regarded as the founder of Kuchipudi?
q.x: Siddhendra Yogi founded Kuchipudi; Adibhatla Narayana Dasu is the father of Harikatha.

q.s: Shaik Nazar is known as the 'Pitamaha' of which art form?
q.x: Shaik Nazar is the Pitamaha of Burrakatha (Padma Shri 1986).

q.s: Budithi in Srikakulam district is famous for:
q.x: Budithi bell and brass craft got GI in 2008; Narasapur is known for crochet lace.

q.s: Which of the following craft–place pairs of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Bell and brass craft is from Budithi, Srikakulam; Kondapalli is known for wooden toys.

q.s: 'Idital' wall paintings are associated with which tribe?
q.x: Idital paintings belong to the Savaras; Pithora is of the Rathwas and Warli of Maharashtra.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a tribal painting tradition?
q.x: Kalamkari is a hand-painted and block-printed textile craft; the other three are tribal wall-painting traditions.

q.s: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in:
q.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873; it inspired the Adi-Andhra leaders.

q.s: Who wrote 'Viswambhara', which won the Jnanpith Award?
q.x: Viswambhara is by C. Narayana Reddy; Viswanatha Satyanarayana wrote Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu and Ravuri Bharadwaja Paakudu Raallu.

q.s: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1969)?
q.x: Devika Rani was the first recipient in 1969.

q.s: Who is hailed as the 'godfather of the Telugu talkie'?
q.x: H.M. Reddy, who assisted Ardeshir Irani on Alam Ara, made the first Telugu talkie Bhakta Prahlada (1931).

q.s: Who chaired the Steering Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
q.x: Rajendra Prasad chaired the Steering Committee; Nehru chaired the States Committee and Patel the Advisory Committee.

q.s: Which material was mainly used by the Amaravati school of art?
q.x: Amaravati used white marble; red sandstone belongs to Mathura and grey schist to Gandhara.

q.s: In temple architecture, the 'Antarala' refers to:
q.x: The antarala is the vestibule between the garbhagriha and the mandapa; the vimana is the tower over the sanctum.

q.s: Who was the founder of the independent Yadava kingdom of Devagiri?
q.x: Bhillama V founded the independent Yadava kingdom; Singhana II was its greatest ruler.

q.s: Which sociologist held that the Indian joint family changes in structure but continues in function?
q.x: A.M. Shah held that the spread of nuclear households does not mean rejection of the joint-family ideal.

q.s: Who is called the 'Father of Modern Sociology'?
q.x: Emile Durkheim is called the Father of Modern Sociology; he gave the concept of anomie (normlessness).

q.s: Durkheim's sacred-profane distinction is found in which work?
o: The Division of Labour in Society
The Elementary Forms of Religious Life
q.x: The sacred-profane distinction is in The Elementary Forms of Religious Life.

q.s: Census 2027 will be India's first digital Census and the first caste count since:
q.x: Census 2027 will be the first full caste count since 1931.

q.s: Operation All Clear (2003) against ULFA was conducted in:
q.x: Operation All Clear was conducted by the Royal Bhutan Army in Bhutan; Bajrang (1990) and Rhino (1991) were in Assam.

q.s: Which of the following military operations was NOT directed against ULFA?
q.x: Operation Blue Star (1984) was against Khalistani militants in Punjab.

q.s: The feminist journal 'Manushi' is associated with:
q.x: Madhu Kishwar founded Manushi; Vina Mazumdar is linked with CWDS.

q.s: Jyotiba Phule started the first girls' school in 1848 at:
q.x: Phule's first girls' school (1848) was in Pune.

q.s: B.R. Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in:
q.x: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was founded in 1924.

q.s: Freedom of religion is guaranteed under which Articles of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: Articles 25-28 cover freedom of religion; Articles 29-30 cover cultural and educational rights.

q.s: The voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age; the 52nd (1985) dealt with anti-defection.

q.s: According to Durkheim, 'anomic suicide' results from:
q.x: Anomic suicide arises from too little regulation (normlessness); fatalistic from too much regulation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Durkheim's types of suicide?
q.x: Durkheim's four types are egoistic, altruistic, anomic and fatalistic.

q.s: Under the Child Labour law as amended in 2016, employing a child is punishable with imprisonment of:
q.x: It is punishable with 6 months to 2 years; offences are cognizable.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the child labour law as amended in 2016 is correct?
o: Parents are punished even for a first offence
Enforcement lies with the Centre alone
q.x: Offences are cognizable; parents are not punished for a first offence.

q.s: In India, which social group has the highest incidence of poverty?
q.x: Scheduled Tribes have the highest incidence of poverty, followed by Scheduled Castes.

q.s: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is implemented by which Ministry?
q.x: NSAP (1995) is under the Ministry of Rural Development and gives effect to Article 41, a Directive Principle.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Social Assistance Programme is correct?
o: It is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
It gives effect to a Fundamental Right
Its National Family Benefit Scheme helps on the death of a breadwinner aged 18-59
q.x: NSAP (1995) is under the Ministry of Rural Development and gives effect to Article 41, a Directive Principle.

q.s: Under the SC/ST (PoA) Amendment Act, 2015, trial in an Exclusive Special Court is to be completed within:
q.x: Trial is to be completed within two months (60 days) of the charge-sheet.

q.s: Nepal's monarchy was abolished by its first Constituent Assembly in:
q.x: The monarchy was abolished on 28 May 2008; the new Constitution was adopted on 20 September 2015.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Nepal is correct?
o: Its new Constitution was adopted on 20 September 2015
Prachanda belonged to the Nepali Congress
q.x: The monarchy was abolished in 2008; Prachanda led the CPN (Maoist).

q.s: In August 2025 the USA doubled its duty on Indian goods to 50 per cent as a penalty for India's purchases of:
q.x: The 50% duty from 27 August 2025 penalised purchases of Russian oil.

q.s: The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) is headquartered at:
q.x: IFAD is in Rome (1977); UPU is in Bern and UNIDO in Vienna.

q.s: Which of the following UN agencies is NOT headquartered in Rome?
q.x: UNIDO is headquartered in Vienna.

q.s: Which country became the 32nd member of NATO in March 2024?
q.x: Sweden joined on 7 March 2024; Finland became the 31st member in April 2023.

q.s: Chabahar port of Iran is located on the:
q.x: Chabahar, in Sistan-Baluchestan, lies on the Gulf of Oman outside the Persian Gulf.

q.s: India develops the Shahid Beheshti terminal of Chabahar through:
q.x: India Ports Global Limited develops the terminal; the 10-year contract was signed in May 2024.

q.s: The strong Centre in the Indian federal system is modelled on the Constitution of:
q.x: The federation with a strong Centre is borrowed from Canada.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian federal system?
q.x: India has single citizenship, unlike the dual citizenship of the USA.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Indian parliamentary system is correct?
o: The Indian Parliament is sovereign like the British Parliament
India has a hereditary head of State
Cases on interpreting the Constitution go to a Bench of at least five judges
Parliament's law-making power is not limited by the Constitution
q.x: A Constitution Bench of at least five judges hears such cases; the Indian Parliament is limited by a written Constitution.

q.s: The criticism of the Indian Constitution as 'elephantine' refers to its:
q.x: 'Elephantine' points to its size; 'bag of borrowings' to its foreign sources and 'lawyers' paradise' to its legalistic language.

q.s: Which mutt is the hereditary Dharmakarta of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams?
q.x: Sri Swamy Hathiramji Mutt is the hereditary Dharmakarta of TTD.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the writ of Quo Warranto is correct?
o: It can be sought only by a person personally aggrieved
It lies only for a substantive public office
It lies for a private office
q.x: Quo Warranto lies only for a substantive public office, and any interested person can seek it.

q.s: Under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, CSR spending must be at least what share of average net profit?
q.x: The CSR floor is 2% of the average net profit of the preceding three years.

q.s: A State Bill imposing restrictions on inter-State trade requires the previous sanction of the:
q.x: Under Article 304(b) such a Bill needs the President's previous sanction.

q.s: Which of the following statements about financial Bills is correct?
o: A Bill imposing a tax needs the President's recommendation
An amendment abolishing a tax needs the President's recommendation
A Bill imposing a tax can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha
A State Bill restricting inter-State trade needs the Governor's sanction
q.x: A tax Bill needs the President's recommendation and is introduced only in the Lok Sabha.

q.s: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
q.x: Collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha only.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Union Council of Ministers is correct?
o: Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President
A Minister from the Rajya Sabha can vote in the Lok Sabha
The Council is collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha
Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Speaker
q.x: Article 75(2): Ministers hold office during the President's pleasure; collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha.

q.s: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

q.s: Seats in the Rajya Sabha are allocated to the States under which Schedule?
q.x: Rajya Sabha seats are allotted by population in the Fourth Schedule.

q.s: Which parliamentary device is considered the most effective method of keeping day-to-day vigil on the executive?
q.x: Question Hour is considered the most effective daily check on the executive.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of parliamentary control over the executive?
q.x: Dissolution is an executive power, not a parliamentary control device.

q.s: Under which Rule of the Lok Sabha is a no-confidence motion moved?
q.x: Rule 198 deals with the no-confidence motion; Rule 193 is short-duration discussion and Rule 377 special mention.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of the Public Account of India?
o: Savings bank deposits are credited to it
Withdrawals from it require an appropriation law
It is operated by executive action
It holds money received in trust
q.x: Public Account payments are made by executive action without a vote of Parliament.

q.s: Which Lok Sabha referred the highest share (71 per cent) of Bills to parliamentary committees?
q.x: The 15th Lok Sabha referred 71 per cent; the 17th referred only 16 per cent.

q.s: Under Article 103, the President decides questions of disqualification of an MP on the opinion of the:
q.x: The President acts on the binding opinion of the Election Commission.

q.s: Which of the following statements about State legislators is correct?
o: A member's resignation takes effect only when accepted by the Speaker or Chairman
Absence for 60 days is a disqualification under Article 191
A person may be a member of both Houses of a State Legislature at once
The Governor decides disqualification on the Speaker's opinion
q.x: A resignation must be accepted; absence for 60 days lets the House declare the seat vacant under Article 190(4).

q.s: The President's salary under the Finance Act, 2018 is:
q.x: The President's salary was raised to ₹5 lakh per month in 2018.

q.s: The President of India addresses his resignation letter to the:
q.x: The President resigns to the Vice-President, who communicates it to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 163 is correct?
o: The Governor's decision on whether a matter is within his discretion is final
The Governor's discretion is narrower than the President's
Courts may inquire into ministerial advice to the Governor
The Council of Ministers advises the Governor in all matters without exception
q.x: Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision final, and the Governor has wider discretion than the President.

q.s: Under Article 254(2), a State law on a Concurrent List subject repugnant to a Union law prevails in the State if:
o: It is passed by two-thirds majority
It is reserved for and receives the President's assent
q.x: A repugnant State law prevails in that State only if it has been reserved for and received the President's assent.

q.s: The Advocate General of a State is appointed under which Article?
q.x: Article 165: the Governor appoints the Advocate General, who holds office during his pleasure.

q.s: Under which Article can the President seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court?
q.x: Article 143 provides advisory jurisdiction; the opinion is not binding on the President.

q.s: Which of the following about the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is NOT correct?
o: The Court may refuse a reference under Article 143(1)
The Court must answer a reference under Article 143(2)
The reference is made by the President
The Court's opinion is binding on the President
q.x: The opinion is advisory and not binding on the President.

q.s: The In-House Procedure (1999) for dealing with misconduct of judges was adopted following which case?
q.x: The In-House Procedure followed C. Ravichandran Iyer (1995).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the removal of a Supreme Court judge is correct?
o: The address needs a majority of total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting
The address needs two-thirds of the total membership of each House
The Chief Justice of India removes the judge
Only the Lok Sabha votes on the address
q.x: A special majority in each House is needed, followed by the President's order.

q.s: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
q.x: M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman judge of the Supreme Court in 1989.

q.s: Where is the Principal Bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal located?
q.x: The CAT's Principal Bench is at New Delhi, with 18 other regular benches.

q.s: Article 258A, enabling a State to entrust its functions to the Union, was inserted by which Amendment?
q.x: Article 258A was inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956.

q.s: Under which Article may a State's failure to comply with Union directions be treated as a breakdown of constitutional machinery?
q.x: Article 365 lets the President treat such failure as a breakdown of constitutional machinery.

q.s: Gyanesh Kumar, who became Chief Election Commissioner in February 2025, succeeded:
q.x: Gyanesh Kumar, the 26th CEC and the first appointed under the 2023 Act, succeeded Rajiv Kumar.

q.s: After the 2014 bifurcation, the headquarters of the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission moved to:
q.x: APPSC headquarters moved to Vijayawada; the Commission has a Chairman and nine Members.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee?
o: Chief Justice of India or his nominee
q.x: The committee is the PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of Opposition, CJI or a nominated judge, and an eminent jurist.

q.s: On which of the following matters is the UPSC NOT consulted?
o: Claims for pension for injuries on duty
Temporary appointments of more than one year
Classification, pay and training of services
q.x: Classification, pay and training are DoPT matters; the UPSC is consulted on the others.

q.s: Which of the following types of audit by the CAG is discretionary?
q.x: Propriety and performance audits are discretionary; compliance and financial attest audits are obligatory.

q.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?
q.x: Justice Ranganath Misra (1993-96) was the first NHRC Chairperson.

q.s: Which Supreme Court case held that inordinate delay in deciding a mercy petition can justify commuting a death sentence?
q.x: Shatrughan Chauhan v Union of India (2014) also held solitary confinement of death-row convicts illegal.

q.s: The Director of the CBI is appointed on the recommendation of a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the:
o: Chief Justice of India or his nominee
q.x: The CBI Director committee is PM, LoP and CJI/nominee; the CVC committee is PM, Home Minister and LoP.

q.s: The committee recommending the Central Vigilance Commissioner does NOT include the:
o: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
q.x: The CVC committee is PM, Home Minister and LoP; the CJI sits on the CBI Director committee.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an All India Service under Article 312 at present?
q.x: The IAS, IPS and Indian Forest Service are the All India Services; the IFS (Foreign) is a Central service.

q.s: Core Centrally Sponsored Schemes for North-Eastern and Himalayan States are funded by the Centre and States in the ratio:
q.x: Core schemes are 60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Centrally Sponsored Schemes is correct?
o: Optional schemes are funded 50:50 for all States without exception
Core schemes are fully funded by the Centre
q.x: Core schemes are mostly 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States); CSS were rationalised in 2015.

q.s: The Swatantra Party was formed in:
q.x: The Swatantra Party was formed in 1959; the Forward Bloc in 1939.

q.s: Superintendence, direction and control of elections is vested in the Election Commission by which Article?
q.x: Article 324 vests elections in the ECI; Article 326 provides adult suffrage and Article 171 deals with Legislative Councils.

q.s: According to the AP Cabinet decision of August 2026, BC reservation in rural local bodies was fixed at:
q.x: BC reservation is 34% in rural and 33⅓% in urban local bodies; the Cabinet also decided on direct election of Mayors.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body for planning at the local level?
q.x: MPLADS is a parallel arrangement bypassing elected local bodies; the others are constitutional bodies.

q.s: Which Article inserted by the 106th Amendment provides for rotation of women's reserved seats after delimitation?
q.x: Article 334A provides for rotation after delimitation; Article 243D(3) reserves one-third of Panchayat seats for women.

q.s: Who among the following is NOT a member of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
q.x: The Governing Council has the PM, all State CMs, CMs of UTs with legislatures and LGs; Governors are not members.

q.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was replaced by the:
q.x: The MRTP Act, enacted on the Dutt Committee's recommendation, was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.

q.s: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework, the inflation target for the RBI is:
q.x: The target is 4% CPI-Combined with a band of ± 2%, set every 5 years.

q.s: What is the term of the external members of the Monetary Policy Committee?
q.x: External MPC members serve a term of 4 years.

q.s: The AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 targets clean energy capacity of:
q.x: The policy targets 160 GW across solar, wind, pumped storage and green hydrogen, and aims at net zero by 2047.

q.s: Greenko's integrated solar-wind-pumped storage project is at:
q.x: The Greenko integrated renewable energy storage project is at Pinnapuram in Kurnool district.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Sevottam is correct?
o: It was begun by the Planning Commission
It has three modules including Citizens' Charter and Public Grievance Redress
Its standard IS 15700:2005 is issued by the Quality Council of India
It is a scheme of NITI Aayog
q.x: Sevottam is a DARPG model with three modules; IS 15700:2005 is a BIS standard.

q.s: Who chaired both the first Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal?
q.x: Justice R.S. Bachawat chaired both; KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar.

q.s: What was the decadal growth rate of India's population during 2001-11?
q.x: Census 2011 put India's population at 121.09 crore with a decadal growth of 17.7%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Census 2011 is correct?
o: Its motto was 'Our Census, Our Future'
The rural share of population was 58.9%
q.x: Census 2011 was the 15th Census, with a rural share of 68.9% and growth of 17.7%.

q.s: The Minimum Needs Programme was launched in which Five Year Plan?
q.x: The Minimum Needs Programme began in 1974, in the Fifth Plan.

q.s: The 'Aarogya Raksha' scheme of Andhra Pradesh (2017) was meant for:
q.x: Aarogya Raksha covered APL families who were outside Aarogyasri.

q.s: How many days of wage work are guaranteed under VB-G RAM G, the Act replacing MGNREGA?
q.x: VB-G RAM G guarantees 125 days, with cost shared 60:40 between the Centre and States.

q.s: What is the total allocation for BC welfare in the AP Budget 2026-27?
q.x: BC welfare (total) is ₹51,021 crore, of which the department gets ₹23,650.88 crore.

q.s: The 'Global Economic Prospects' report is released by the:
q.x: The World Bank releases GEP in January and June; the IMF releases the WEO.

q.s: Which of the following reports is NOT released by the World Bank?
q.x: The World Economic Outlook is the IMF's.

q.s: India's GDP and sectoral GVA estimates are compiled by the:
q.x: The NSO (MoSPI) compiles GDP; State GSDP is compiled by the State DES.

q.s: As per Census 2011, what share of Andhra Pradesh's (13 districts) workers were agricultural labourers?
q.x: Agricultural labourers were 47.9% of AP's workers; cultivators were 14.5%.

q.s: Who built the Human Development Index on Amartya Sen's capability ideas?
q.x: Mahbub ul Haq devised the HDI (UNDP, 1990).

q.s: Which of the following books was NOT written by Amartya Sen?
q.x: A Field of One's Own is by Bina Agarwal; the others are Sen's.

q.s: A Gini coefficient of 1 indicates:
q.x: The Gini ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (one person has all the income).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Gini coefficient is correct?
o: A higher Gini coefficient indicates lower inequality
It is derived from the Phillips curve
A Gini coefficient of 0.40 equals a Gini index of 40
q.x: The Gini index is the coefficient multiplied by 100; it is derived from the Lorenz curve.

q.s: The role of the National Development Council has now passed to the:
q.x: The NDC's role has passed to NITI Aayog's Governing Council.

q.s: In the Harrod-Domar model, the growth rate equals:
q.x: g = s / k, so growth falls as the capital-output ratio rises.

q.s: The Twelfth Five Year Plan set an Infant Mortality Rate target of:
q.x: The Twelfth Plan set an IMR target of 25.

q.s: What was India's GDP growth rate in the crisis year 1990-91?
q.x: GDP growth fell to 1.1%; the Centre's gross fiscal deficit was 8.4% of GDP.

q.s: The 14th Finance Commission gave its rural local-body grants only to:
q.x: The 14th FC gave rural grants only to gram panchayats, with a 90:10 basic-to-performance ratio.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a condition for release of Finance Commission grants to local bodies?
o: Special Category Status of the State
q.x: The grants require elected bodies, audited accounts and SFC compliance; Special Category Status is irrelevant.

q.s: Prime Minister Manmohan Singh announced Special Category Status for AP for five years on 20 February 2014 in the:
q.x: The SCS assurance was given in the Rajya Sabha and was not written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

q.s: Under which Section of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 can banks undertake para-banking activities with RBI approval?
q.x: Section 6 lists permitted businesses (RBI approval needed); Section 19(1) provides the subsidiary route.

q.s: IDBI was set up in July 1964 as a subsidiary of the:
q.x: IDBI began as an RBI subsidiary; IDBI Bank became a private sector bank after LIC's 2019 takeover.

q.s: ICICI, set up in 1955 in the joint sector, was established on the initiative of the:
q.x: ICICI was set up on a World Bank initiative and later became a universal bank.

q.s: NABARD was set up on:
q.x: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981.

q.s: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) managed by NABARD is funded by:
q.x: RIDF is funded by banks' shortfalls in priority-sector lending.

q.s: The practice of giving fresh loans to a borrower to repay old ones, hiding default, is called:
q.x: Evergreening hides default by rolling over loans; Net NPA is Gross NPA minus provisions.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a typical restriction imposed on a bank under the RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework?
o: Mandatory doubling of deposit interest rates
q.x: PCA curbs lending, branch expansion, dividends and management pay; it does not mandate deposit rates.

q.s: The 'displacement effect' in public expenditure theory is associated with:
q.x: The Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis (1961), based on UK data, gave the displacement effect; Wagner gave the law of increasing state activity.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Wagner's law is correct?
o: Public spending rises faster than national income as an economy industrialises
Public spending rises slower than national income
It is also called the displacement effect
It was based on UK data of the World Wars
q.x: Wagner's law of increasing state activity holds that public spending rises faster than income; the displacement effect is Peacock-Wiseman's.

q.s: Which of the following agencies did NOT upgrade India's sovereign rating in 2025?
q.x: The three 2025 upgrades came from Morningstar DBRS, S&P and R&I.

q.s: The technique of budgeting in which every scheme is justified afresh with no base from the previous year is called:
q.x: Zero-based budgeting (Peter Pyhrr) justifies every item afresh; the outcome budget sets outlays against measurable results.

q.s: The Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme (VDIS) was launched in:
q.x: VDIS was launched in 1997; the Income Declaration Scheme came in 2016.

q.s: In June 1966 the rupee was devalued under the government of:
q.x: The June 1966 devaluation (₹4.76 to ₹7.50 per dollar) was under Indira Gandhi's government.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the rupee's devaluations is correct?
o: The 1966 devaluation was under the Janata Government
The first devaluation was in September 1949, along with sterling
The 1991 devaluation was done in a single step
The rupee was never devalued before 1991
q.x: The 1949 devaluation was of about 30.5%; the 1991 devaluation came in two steps.

q.s: The IMF created Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) in:
q.x: SDRs were created in 1969 to supplement members' reserves; the renminbi joined the basket in 2016.

q.s: The largest general allocation of SDRs, about $650 billion, was made in:
q.x: The August 2021 allocation was made during the COVID-19 crisis.

q.s: Devaluation of a currency is an example of which kind of policy?
q.x: Devaluation is expenditure-switching: it lowers foreign-currency prices of exports and raises import prices.

q.s: Which is the largest land-use category in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Net area sown is largest, followed by forests; miscellaneous tree crops is the smallest.

q.s: The National Agriculture Policy, 2000 targeted an agricultural growth rate of over:
q.x: NAP 2000 targeted over 4% growth and envisaged a 'Rainbow Revolution'.

q.s: The AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 came into force on:
q.x: The 1973 Act, under P.V. Narasimha Rao, took the family of five as the unit and came into force on 1 January 1975.

q.s: Which of the following statements about land ceiling laws in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The 1961 Act took the family as the unit
The 1973 Act took the individual as the unit
The 1973 Act took a family of five as the unit
The 1973 Act came into force in 1980
q.x: The 1961 Act took the individual; the 1973 Act took a family of five and came into force on 1 January 1975.

q.s: NABARD provides agricultural credit mainly by way of:
o: Refinance to cooperative banks, RRBs and commercial banks
q.x: NABARD is an apex refinancing institution and does not lend crop credit directly to farmers.

q.s: Where is the headquarters of the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)?
q.x: SIDBI is headquartered at Lucknow; KVIC is at Mumbai.

q.s: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) is headquartered at:
q.x: KVIC is at Mumbai and runs PMEGP.

q.s: The AP Socio-Economic Survey is presented by:
q.x: The SES is the Andhra Pradesh Government's own survey; growth figures in SES 2025-26 are First Advance Estimates.

q.s: Who presented the first budget of residuary Andhra Pradesh in 2014-15?
q.x: Yanamala Ramakrishnudu presented the 2014-15 budget.

q.s: Which State ranks first in India in oil-palm area?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh has about 48% of India's oil-palm area and leads in productivity too.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, land for industries is allotted by:
q.x: APIIC (incorporated 1973) allots land; APIDC and APSFC finance industry.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's coastline (about 1,053 km) is the third longest in India after:
q.x: AP's coastline is third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: IIT Tirupati and IISER Tirupati are both located at:
q.x: Both are at Yerpedu; the NIDM Southern Campus is at Kondapalli.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT promised to Andhra Pradesh in the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: The Thirteenth Schedule lists IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, AIIMS and others but no NIFT.

q.s: Under the SEZ Rules 2006, a multi-product SEZ needed a minimum area of:
q.x: A multi-product SEZ needed 1,000 hectares; the 2019 minimum for sector-specific SEZs is 50 hectares.

q.s: The AP Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0 is implemented by:
q.x: It is implemented by the AP Innovation Society and was issued by the ITE&C Department; it targets 1 lakh jobs.

q.s: The Stand-Up India Scheme provides bank loans in the range of:
q.x: Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) gives loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore; its refinance window is through SIDBI.

q.s: The National Health Policy, 2017 targets public health expenditure of what share of GDP by 2025?
q.x: NHP 2017 targets 2.5% of GDP.

q.s: Which colour of stars indicates the highest surface temperature?
q.x: Blue stars are the hottest and red stars the coolest; the Sun is a yellow star.

q.s: The absolute magnitude of a star is its brightness as seen from a distance of:
q.x: Absolute magnitude is measured at 10 parsecs; a lower magnitude means a brighter star.

q.s: Which planet has the highest mean density in the Solar System?
q.x: The Earth's mean density is about 5.5 g/cm³, the highest of all planets.

q.s: Which State holds about 90% of India's diamond reserves?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh (Panna) holds about 90% of reserves.

q.s: Mica (muscovite) belongs to which silicate structural class?
q.x: Micas are sheet silicates, which is why they split into thin sheets; feldspars and quartz are framework silicates.

q.s: Which of the following minerals is NOT a framework silicate (tectosilicate)?
q.x: Muscovite (mica) is a sheet silicate; quartz and the feldspars are framework silicates.

q.s: Which of the following is an active factor of soil formation?
q.x: Climate and biological activity are active factors; parent material, topography and time are passive.

q.s: The world's largest mangrove forest is the:
q.x: The Sundarbans in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta form the largest mangrove forest; about two-thirds of the delta is in Bangladesh.

q.s: A crescent-shaped sand dune with its horns pointing downwind is called a:
q.x: A barchan is crescent-shaped; seifs are long longitudinal dunes and a playa is a dry salt-lake bed.

q.s: Which of the following landforms is NOT formed by wind action?
q.x: A drumlin is a glacial landform.

q.s: The island of Socotra belongs to:
q.x: Socotra belongs to Yemen; Svalbard, home of India's Himadri station, belongs to Norway.

q.s: India's Arctic research station 'Himadri' is located in:
q.x: Himadri is at Ny-Alesund in Svalbard, Norway.

q.s: Lake Nyasa is another name for:
q.x: Lake Malawi, at the southern end of the rift chain, is also called Lake Nyasa.

q.s: Which of the following lakes does NOT lie in the western (Albertine) branch of the Great Rift Valley?
q.x: Lake Victoria lies in the basin between the two branches.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the polar vortex is correct?
o: It is a warm high-pressure region over the poles
When weakened, it can spill cold air into the mid-latitudes
It rotates clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere
q.x: The polar vortex is a cold low-pressure region, strongest in winter, rotating anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.

q.s: The Coriolis force is maximum at the:
q.x: The Coriolis force is zero at the equator and maximum at the poles; it deflects winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.

q.s: Which of the following statements about humidity is NOT correct?
o: Water vapour in the air increases with latitude
Relative humidity is higher over oceans than over continents
Warm air can hold more water vapour than cold air
Relative humidity is expressed as a percentage
q.x: Water vapour decreases from the equator towards the poles.

q.s: Kerala's 'red rain' phenomenon was observed in:
q.x: Kerala's red rain fell in 2001; such blood rain comes from dust or spores in raindrops.

q.s: The Polar Front Theory of temperate cyclones was put forward by:
q.x: The Bjerknes father and son of the Bergen School, Norway, gave the Polar Front Theory.

q.s: The 'Damini' mobile application gives alerts for:
q.x: Damini, developed by IITM Pune, gives lightning alerts.

q.s: According to the DST climate vulnerability report (2021), which is the most vulnerable State in India?
q.x: Jharkhand is the most vulnerable State; Assam is among the eight highly vulnerable States.

q.s: The 2023-24 remeasurement of India's coastline was carried out by the National Hydrographic Office and the:
q.x: It was carried out by the NHO and the Survey of India; it counted 1,389 islands.

q.s: Which district has the longest coastline in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Srikakulam has AP's longest district coastline (about 193 km).

q.s: The Narmada river flows between which two ranges?
q.x: The Narmada flows west in a rift between the Vindhya (north) and the Satpura (south).

q.s: Amarkantak in the Maikal Range is the source of the Narmada and the:
q.x: Amarkantak is the source of the Narmada and the Son; the Tapi rises at Multai.

q.s: How many districts of Andhra Pradesh touch the coast as per the 2022 district map?
q.x: In the 2022 map 12 districts touch the coast; West Godavari has the shortest coastline.

q.s: Which of the following hydroelectric projects is NOT located on the Chenab?
q.x: Tehri is on the Bhagirathi; Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti are on the Chenab.

q.s: The Pong reservoir (Maharana Pratap Sagar) is on which river?
q.x: Maharana Pratap Sagar is the Pong reservoir on the Beas.

q.s: At which prayag does the Pindar river join the Alaknanda?
q.x: The Pindar joins at Karnaprayag; the Mandakini joins at Rudraprayag.

q.s: At Devprayag, the Alaknanda meets which river to form the Ganga?
q.x: The Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet at Devprayag to form the Ganga.

q.s: The Pranhita, the largest tributary of the Godavari, joins it at:
q.x: The Pranhita (Wainganga, Wardha and Penganga) joins the Godavari at Kaleshwaram in Telangana.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Godavari's tributaries is correct?
o: The Pranhita is formed by the Wainganga, Wardha and Penganga
The Pranhita joins the Godavari at Polavaram
The Manjira is a left-bank tributary
The Sabari is a tributary of the Krishna
q.x: The Manjira is a right-bank tributary; the Pranhita joins at Kaleshwaram; the Sabari joins the Godavari.

q.s: The Tammileru river drains into:
q.x: The Tammileru drains into Kolleru Lake.

q.s: National Waterway-4 runs from:
q.x: NW-4 runs from Kakinada to Puducherry along the Godavari, Krishna and Buckingham Canal.

q.s: The Kurnool-Cuddapah (KC) Canal was built by:
q.x: The KC Canal was built by the private Madras Irrigation and Canal Company.

q.s: The North Coastal agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is typified by which soil?
q.x: The North Coastal zone has laterite soil due to heavy rainfall and leaching.

q.s: The deadliest cyclone in Andhra Pradesh (1977) struck:
q.x: The 1977 cyclone struck Diviseema in Krishna district.

q.s: Tsunami inundation modelling in India is done by:
q.x: INCOIS, Hyderabad, runs the tsunami early warning centre; drought is monitored through NADAMS.

q.s: In MADA v. SAIL (2024), the Supreme Court held that royalty on minerals is:
q.x: The Court held that royalty is not a tax, so States can tax mineral rights.

q.s: For auctioned mining leases, miners pay what share of royalty to the District Mineral Foundation?
q.x: They pay 10% for auctioned leases and 30% for old leases.

q.s: Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar and Jawahar Sagar dams are on which river?
q.x: These dams are on the Chambal, the main tributary of the Yamuna.

q.s: Which of the following dams is NOT on the Chambal river?

q.s: The seated Dharmachakrapravartana Buddha found at Sarnath belongs to which period?
q.x: It is a Gupta-period work; the Dhamek Stupa marks the first sermon.

q.s: The Paris Agreement was adopted at:
q.x: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP 21 in 2015.

q.s: National Panchayati Raj Day (24 April) marks:
o: Coming into force of the 73rd Amendment
Passing of the 73rd Amendment in Parliament
Launch of the Balwantrai Mehta report
q.x: It marks the 73rd Amendment coming into force on 24 April 1993; PAI 2.0 is prepared by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.

q.s: Kumbhalgarh Fort in Rajasthan was built by:
q.x: Rana Kumbha built it in the 15th century; Maharana Pratap was born there.

q.s: The Ramsar Convention on wetlands was adopted in:
q.x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted on 2 February 1971; World Wetlands Day is 2 February.

q.s: The Indian Coast Guard was established in:
q.x: The Coast Guard was established in 1977 and marked its 50th Raising Day on 1 February 2026.

q.s: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi was sentenced in 2026 by the:
q.x: Thaçi was sentenced by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers at The Hague.

q.s: The title 'Vishva Vaidya Divyang Bandhu' was conferred on Dr Guduru Jagadish by the Prime Minister of:
q.x: Mauritius PM Ramgoolam conferred it for his free polio surgery camps.

q.s: Under the Bihar-Jharkhand Son river agreement, Bihar's share is:
q.x: Bihar gets 5.75 MAF and Jharkhand 2.0 MAF of the 7.75 MAF under the Bansagar Agreement.

q.s: The Son river is a:
q.x: The Son rises on the Amarkantak Plateau and is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga.

q.s: Who is the Governor of Telangana who promulgated the October 2026 judicial-officers ordinance?
q.x: Shiv Pratap Shukla is the Telangana Governor; Arlekar went to Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026 amends which Schedule of the Constitution?
q.x: It amends the First Schedule under Article 3.

q.s: Under the Public Examinations Amendment Act 2026, organised paper-leak crime is punishable with imprisonment of:
q.x: Organised crime carries 7 to 10 years and a fine up to Rs 10 crore.

q.s: The Sabarimala temple is administered by the:
q.x: Sabarimala is run by the Travancore Devaswom Board.

q.s: Who gave the lone dissent in the 2018 Sabarimala verdict?
q.x: Justice Indu Malhotra dissented in the 4:1 verdict.

q.s: The Governor's address to the State Legislature is provided under which Article?
q.x: Article 176 provides the Governor's special address; it traces back to Section 63 of the GoI Act, 1935.

q.s: Under the NDPS Act, 1985, 'charas' means:
q.x: Charas is cannabis resin; ganja is the flowering or fruiting tops; bhang is left to the States.

q.s: The 129th Constitution Amendment Bill (2024) on One Nation One Election proposes to insert:
q.x: The 129th Bill inserts Article 82A; Article 334A was inserted by the 106th (women's reservation).

q.s: The SME Growth Fund approved in October 2026 carries a government commitment of:
q.x: The Rs 10,000 crore fund, announced in Budget 2026-27, is a SEBI-regulated AIF investing in SMEs.

q.s: The Clydebank Declaration on green shipping corridors was launched at:
q.x: The Clydebank Declaration was launched at COP26, Glasgow, 2021.

q.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets green hydrogen production of how much by 2030?
q.x: The mission targets 5 million metric tonnes a year by 2030.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the World Bank Group?
q.x: The World Bank Group is IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID; the BIS is a separate body at Basel.

q.s: The IMF's World Economic Outlook is published:
o: Twice a year, in April and October
q.x: The WEO comes out in April and October.

q.s: 'American upland cotton' refers to which species?
q.x: G. hirsutum is American upland cotton; G. herbaceum and G. arboreum are Asian (desi) cottons.

q.s: 'Namo Drone Didi', which gives agri-drones to women SHGs, is a:
q.x: Namo Drone Didi is a Central Sector scheme, fully funded by the Centre.

q.s: The 'sacrifice ratio' in monetary economics refers to:
o: Bank capital lost per bad loan
GDP lost per one point fall in inflation
q.x: The sacrifice ratio is the output lost for each point of disinflation.

q.s: India's record peak power demand of 256.1 GW on 25 April 2026 was met mainly by:
q.x: Coal met about 66.9% and solar about 21.5% of the peak.

q.s: India's annual consumption of urea is about:
q.x: India uses about 39-40 million tonnes of urea a year.

q.s: The headquarters of IRDAI is located at:
q.x: IRDAI (1999) is headquartered in Hyderabad.

q.s: What is the FDI limit in the insurance sector after the 2025 amendment?
q.x: 100% FDI is allowed in insurance; the foreign cap in LIC stays at 20%.

q.s: The Shilp Samagam Mela for artisans is organised by the Ministry of:
q.x: Shilp Samagam is organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of DISHA 2.0 (2026-31)?
q.x: DISHA 2.0 has Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, Legal Literacy & Awareness and Vidhi-Sanjeevani.

q.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) was established in:
q.x: The IBBI was set up on 1 October 2016 under the IBC, 2016.

q.s: 'SWAYATT' is an initiative of:
q.x: SWAYATT is a GeM initiative for startups, women and youth; Gruha Sugam is NHB's portal.

q.s: Under Namo Drone Didi, women SHGs get a subsidy of what share of the cost of agri-drones (up to ₹8 lakh)?
q.x: SHGs get an 80% subsidy up to ₹8 lakh.

q.s: Under PM MUDRA Yojana, the 'Kishor' category covers loans of:
q.x: Kishor covers ₹50,001-5 lakh; Shishu up to ₹50,000 and Tarun ₹5-10 lakh.

q.s: The 'Tarun Plus' category of MUDRA loans covers loans of:
q.x: Tarun Plus covers ₹10-20 lakh.

q.s: Under the restructured PM SVANidhi, the first loan tranche has been raised to:
q.x: The first tranche rose from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000 and the second to ₹25,000.

q.s: Who chairs the Department-Related Standing Committee on External Affairs (2026)?
q.x: Shashi Tharoor chairs External Affairs; Bhartruhari Mahtab chairs Finance.

q.s: Who chaired the JPC on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024?
q.x: Jagdambika Pal chaired the Waqf Bill JPC.

q.s: The Lead Bank Scheme was introduced in:
q.x: The Lead Bank Scheme began in 1969; the RBI was set up in 1935.

q.s: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority was established in:
q.x: NPPA was set up in 1997; the Department of Pharmaceuticals in 2008.

q.s: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre-State relations was set up by the government of:
q.x: It was set up by the Tamil Nadu government; the Inter-State Council came in 1990.

q.s: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats?
q.x: Anamudi is the highest; Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris.

q.s: Pulicat Lake is shared by Andhra Pradesh and:
q.x: Pulicat is shared by AP and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The international basis of Geographical Indication (GI) protection is the WTO agreement on:
q.x: GI protection rests on TRIPS.

q.s: The IMD defines a cloudburst as rainfall of more than how much in one hour over about 20-30 sq km?
q.x: A cloudburst is more than 100 mm of rain in one hour over about 20-30 sq km.

q.s: The Northeast monsoon gives about what share of Tamil Nadu's annual rainfall?
q.x: It gives about 48% of Tamil Nadu's and over 30% of AP's annual rain.

q.s: The final of the ICC Women's ODI World Cup 2025 was played at:
q.x: India beat South Africa by 52 runs at the DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai.

q.s: Whom did India defeat in the final of the ICC Women's ODI World Cup 2025?
q.x: India beat South Africa by 52 runs; India had lost the finals of 2005 and 2017.

q.s: Protection of Good Samaritans who help road accident victims is provided under Section 134A of the:
q.x: Section 134A is in the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

q.s: How many districts has Andhra Pradesh had since 31 December 2025?
q.x: AP has 28 districts since 31 December 2025, including Markapuram and Polavaram.

q.s: Under the amended GSWS Act, Grama Sachivalayams in Andhra Pradesh were renamed:
q.x: They were renamed Swarna Gramam.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's Talliki Vandanam scheme was earlier known as:
q.x: Talliki Vandanam was earlier Amma Vodi and is run by the School Education Department.

q.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 inserts the words 'at Amaravati' in which Section of the 2014 Act?
q.x: It amends Section 5(2), with effect from 2 June 2024.

q.s: Under the Gross Cost Contract model for APSRTC's electric buses:
o: APSRTC owns and maintains the buses
The private operator owns the buses and is paid per km
q.x: Under GCC the private operator owns and maintains the buses and is paid per km.

q.s: The Divyang Shakti free bus travel scheme of Andhra Pradesh does NOT cover which services?
q.x: It covers City Ordinary, Palle Velugu and Express buses but not AC or luxury services.

q.s: In Q1 2025-26, which sector had the largest output value in Andhra Pradesh's economy?
q.x: Services were ₹1,57,321 crore, the largest; industry was ₹92,843 crore.

q.s: About 70-80% of malaria cases in Andhra Pradesh are caused by:
q.x: P. falciparum causes most of AP's malaria; the vector is the female Anopheles mosquito.

q.s: Orvakal Drone City is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Orvakal is in Kurnool district; Drone City covers 600 acres of the 2,621-acre node.

q.s: Which is India's National Heritage Animal?
q.x: The Asian elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010.

q.s: The Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary, a critical elephant habitat, is in which region of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Koundinya is in the Chittoor area, where AP's elephants are concentrated.

q.s: India's first large-scale indigenous green urea plant at Poodimadaka is under an MoU between Asago Industries and:
q.x: The plant (1,000 tonnes per day) is with NTPC Green Energy; AM Green's green ammonia plant is at Kakinada.

q.s: Polavaram was declared a national project under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: Section 90 declared Polavaram a national project, so the Union bears its cost.

q.s: Sarla Aviation's 'Sky Factory', India's first giga-scale eVTOL ecosystem, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Sky Factory is in Anantapur; its flagship hybrid VTOL is 'Shunya'.

q.s: The proposed Chelam Hill thermal power project of APGENCO is in which district?
q.x: The 3,200 MW project is in Srikakulam; water is to come from the Vamsadhara.

q.s: Which one of the following institution–location pairs in Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: NID is at Amaravati, not Tirupati.

q.s: The Samvatsara cycle associated with Ugadi consists of how many years?
q.x: The cycle has 60 named years; Ugadi falls on the first day of Chaitra.

q.s: The Central Silk Board functions under the Ministry of:
q.x: The Central Silk Board (1948) is under the Ministry of Textiles.
